title: Special Card
description: The offer panel the live Specials archive renders — one full-width band per special, the property photograph as the band's ground with a dark panel of copy held against one edge of it. Measured from `.post-type-archive-lsx-to-special #primary .lsx-to-archive-item` on 2026-09-17: the band is 540px tall with the photograph set `background-size: cover`; the panel is 460px wide, full band height, `rgba(26,18,5,0.8)` over it, its copy left-aligned; the title is #E6AD10 Joe Hand 36px weight 300; the enquiry button is #CC7F16, 336px wide. Bands butt straight together — `.lsx-to-archive-item { margin: 0 }` — and the panel alternates leading edge, trailing edge, leading edge down the page. Structure (2026-09-17): the photograph is absolutely positioned inside the band and the panel sits in normal flow, so the band is never shorter than 540px and never shorter than its own copy — a long offer grows the band instead of overflowing it, at every width and with no media query, which this `css` field would silently unwrap anyway. The band paints a neutral-900 ground of its own: that is the no-image fallback, since `core/post-featured-image` renders nothing at all for an offer with no featured image and the panel would otherwise set base-coloured text over the page. **The band's two children are addressed as blocks, not by class.** `& > .wp-block-post-featured-image` and `& > .wp-block-group` replaced the hand-rolled `special-card__media` / `special-card__body` classes on 2026-09-17; the band holds exactly one image and exactly one group, so the block selectors are as precise as the classes were and an editor rebuilding the band by hand gets the layout for free. The unused `special-card__badge` rules went with them. What is not here: the panel's scrim, the edge alternation, the sub-900px stack and the offer-copy size normalisation all live in `assets/styles/core-group.css`. The scrim has to sit over the photograph rather than behind it, the alternation keys off `li:nth-child(even)` above the band, the stack is an `@media`, and the size rule has to out-specify `theme.json`'s own `:root :where(p)` in both environments — none of the four can be expressed here.

styles.css: & { position: relative; display: flex; overflow: hidden; min-height: 540px; } & > .wp-block-post-featured-image { position: absolute; inset: 0; margin: 0 !important; line-height: 0; } & > .wp-block-post-featured-image img { width: 100%; height: 100%; object-fit: cover; } & > .wp-block-group { position: relative; margin: 0 !important; display: flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: center; width: 100%; max-width: 460px; padding: var(--wp--preset--spacing--30) var(--wp--preset--spacing--40) var(--wp--preset--spacing--50); } & > .wp-block-group p { line-height: var(--wp--custom--line-height--body); }
